result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. They default to 30, can be set at registration and changed later, and show up in every supplier listing and the single lookup. The full `mvn -q -o test` run passes.

- **`schema.sql`**: new `supplier.payment_terms_days` column, `INT DEFAULT 30 NOT NULL CHECK (> 0)`.
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: the record has a new last component, `paymentTermsDays`. I kept the old 5-argument constructor, which uses the standard 30 days, so existing callers and tests compile unchanged.
- **`DataStore.java`**: `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` write the terms, which covers renegotiation. `listSuppliersByName`, `listSuppliersByCountry`, `listSuppliersByMinimumRating` and `findSupplierById` read them. I also updated the other queries that build a `Supplier` inside report rows (spending, performance, purchased quantity, category suppliers, supplier products), so they show the real terms rather than a default 30.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: two new tests. One checks the 30-day default. The other registers a Swedish supplier at 45 days, renegotiates it to 14, and checks 14 in the lookup and all three listings.

There's no service layer for suppliers, so nothing was added there, and I didn't add a separate "change terms" method. Renegotiating goes through the existing `updateSupplier`.
